ModuleName: Controlled User Testing and Data Collection
CourseName: CEN3722 - Introduction to Human Computer Interfaces

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: A structured outline of the module's core topics—covering experimental design fundamentals, participant recruitment, task scenario writing, data collection methods, and usability metrics—that guides both instructors in planning lessons and learners in understanding what concepts and skills the module will address.

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics (HTML)
Artifacts.Description: A navigation page listing the topics covered in the Controlled User Testing and Data Collection module — including experimental design principles, variables, controls, and study validity — which learners use to orient themselves and access specific subject areas within the module.

Artifacts.Name: Foundations of Experimental Design for Usability Testing
Artifacts.Description: This reading introduces core experimental design concepts for usability studies, covering how to define research questions, select variables, choose study structures, and make the key decisions needed before testing begins, serving as foundational theory for the module.

Artifacts.Name: Participant Selection and Recruitment
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains how to identify, screen, and recruit appropriate test participants, covering sampling strategies, screener design, and why participant representativeness is critical to the validity of usability study findings.

Artifacts.Name: Task Scenario Scripting
Artifacts.Description: This reading covers how to write effective task scenarios for usability tests, explaining what makes a scenario realistic and motivating, common scripting pitfalls to avoid, and how scenario quality directly affects the behavioral data collected.

Artifacts.Name: Think-Aloud Protocol
Artifacts.Description: This reading describes the think-aloud protocol method, explaining how to instruct participants to verbalize their thoughts during tasks, the difference between concurrent and retrospective approaches, and how facilitators use it to capture real-time user reasoning.

Artifacts.Name: Quantitative Data Collection
Artifacts.Description: This reading covers quantitative data collection in usability testing, explaining what numerical metrics such as task completion rates, time-on-task, and error counts measure, how to record them consistently, and how they are used to compare and benchmark interface performance.

Artifacts.Name: Qualitative Data Collection
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains qualitative data collection methods in usability testing, covering observational note-taking, verbal data capture, and how these techniques reveal the reasons behind user behavior to complement numerical metrics.

Artifacts.Name: Conducting Live User Testing Sessions
Artifacts.Description: This reading guides facilitators through running live usability test sessions, covering session structure, facilitator conduct, how to manage participants without biasing results, and practical considerations for both in-person and remote testing contexts.

Artifacts.Name: Compiling Structured Results for Analysis
Artifacts.Description: This reading explains how to organize and structure raw usability test data — including notes, metrics, transcripts, and questionnaire scores — into formats suitable for systematic analysis, covering data cleaning, categorization, and preparation techniques.
